title: Have Pity, Lord, for Thou Are Great
description: Have Pity, Lord, for Thou Are Great in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Greek Office Books (Paisley, 1904).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Have pi-ty, Lord, for Thou are great, And great-ness pi-ty knows; I mourn my poor and worth-less state, And all its wants and woes.

lines: Have pity, Lord, for Thou are great,
I mourn my poor and worthless state,
And all its wants and woes.
Have pity, Lord, for Thou art great; —
I would from sin be free,
And seek Thy face, 'though coming late,
Have pity, Lord, for Thou art great,
And give me strength to win;
That I may gain the heavenly gate
Have pity, Lord, for Thou art love,
I hope in Thy pure house above

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Greek Office Books (1904)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Greek Office Books; set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
